D011-D018_h001.question: Lately, it feels like I’m always on edge, jumpy at the slightest noise. I’ve been worrying constantly for what feels like forever; it’s hard to put a number on it, but it’s definitely been over six months. My husband says I fret about everything, and he’s not wrong. Even little things, like the numbers for the census not adding up perfectly or if I've remembered to lock the door, become huge in my head. I try to tell myself to stop, to just let it go, but the thoughts just loop, almost like a broken record. My jaw is almost always sore and tense, especially by the end of the day, to the point where I get these throbbing headaches. Sometimes I wonder if it’s all tied to something that happened a while back, something awful, but it’s hard to say for sure. Even without thinking about that, the worry is just… always there.

A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
D011-D018_h001.answer: A & B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D011-D018_h002.question: "I'm here because… well, things just aren’t right. It’s been about six months now, maybe a bit longer. My whole body feels like a coiled spring, and my jaw… I wake up with headaches and a sore jaw almost every morning from clenching my teeth all night. I keep replaying that car accident from last year – it was bad, a head-on collision, though thankfully everyone walked away seemingly okay. I just can't seem to shake it, and everything feels so precarious since then."

    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
